lastCompletedStory.title: Add the derived parity check script and bring templates/.gitignore to parity

nextStoryContext: US-002 added scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh (GOTCHA 1 derivation copied verbatim from the CAM-502 issue, plus a PROBES=<n> non-vacuity line and a fail-closed guard on zero derived probes) and brought templates/.gitignore to parity with the repo's own .gitignore: added the 16 rules that were diverging (13 pre-existing plus the 3 US-001 added to the repo root). Verified live: `bash scripts/check-gitignore-parity.sh .` prints PROBES=42 and exits 0 with no DIVERGE lines; the fail-closed guard was swept against a throwaway repo holding only a copy of templates/.gitignore and no src/ (exits non-zero, PROBES=0). embed-vendor regenerated + embed-vendor:check clean in the same commit. AC3 of the CAM-502 issue spec (a durable bun-test exercising materializeTemplates over git check-ignore, covering both the verbatim-write and mergeGitignore paths) is issue-spec scope, not literally required by this PRD's US-002 acceptanceCriteria list (which only requires the shell oracle itself, its non-vacuity/fail-closed behavior, its anti-regression, its header, template parity, typecheck and bun test) -- if a later story in this PRD (or a review round) expects that durable test, it is not yet written; check prd.json for a US-003/US-004 that may own it before assuming it's missing by oversight. WHY BASH is recorded in the PRD notes for US-002 as a deliberate trade-off (no biome/knip/type coverage on a .sh) that a hypothetical follow-up story would need to buy back via a bun test driving this script, per the notes on US-002 in prd.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: git check-ignore exit codes confirmed: 0 = at least one path ignored, 1 = none ignored, 128 = fatal error. The script's `[ "$here" -gt 1 ]` / `[ "$tpl" -gt 1 ]` error-collapse (treat anything above 1 as ERROR, never as a verdict) matches this exactly.
